# Summary: calibrated seam scale for VGGT-Long (generated by scripts/make_summary.py)

Written from the files in `results/final/`; numbers are ATE in metres (Sim(3)-aligned), with loops unless stated.
The method was designed at 32/16 on these KITTI drives; 30/15 is a rerun at VGGT-Long's nearest published
setting, not an independent test. The 60/30 and 75/30 evaluation was fixed before its results existed.

## 1. Labels (final_PLAN.md F7) and the claim they allow
- R1 ours 30/15 (auto): **improvement**. mean 45.66 -> 35.35 m (-22.6%), geometric-mean ratio 0.746, 7 better / 3 worse of 11, Wilcoxon p 0.083, worst 01 x1.63, 95% interval of the mean change [-52%, +25%]
- R2 ours 60/30 (auto): **no reliable gain**. mean 25.82 -> 25.00 m (-3.2%), geometric-mean ratio 0.822, 8 better / 3 worse of 11, Wilcoxon p 0.206, worst 03 x1.73, 95% interval of the mean change [-33%, +36%]
- R3 ours 75/30 (auto): **no reliable gain**. mean 24.61 -> 25.37 m (+3.1%), geometric-mean ratio 0.843, 9 better / 2 worse of 11, Wilcoxon p 0.240, worst 03 x1.92, 95% interval of the mean change [-24%, +33%]
- R4 upstream VGGT-Long 30/15 (C4): **clear improvement**. mean 44.70 -> 28.09 m (-37.2%), geometric-mean ratio 0.704, 8 better / 2 worse of 11, Wilcoxon p 0.019, worst 00 x1.15, 95% interval of the mean change [-51%, -15%]
- R5 upstream VGGT-Long 75/30 (C4): **not run in full**; agreement check on five short drives only (part 5).
- Note on R1: `auto` chose C4 for 10 drives and something else for 01 (C1_const: 156.67 m; C4 would give 77.64 m). The C4 row at 30/15: mean 45.66 -> 28.17 m (-38.3%), geometric-mean ratio 0.700, 8 better / 2 worse of 11, Wilcoxon p 0.019, worst 00 x1.16, 95% interval of the mean change [-52%, -15%]. `auto` stays the headline of our pipeline; R4 uses C4, as fixed before.
- Robustness of R4: median ATE 19.53 -> 18.04 m; without the two largest gains (drives 02 and 08) the mean goes 28.00 -> 22.39 m (-20%). The mean gain is carried by the long, high-drift drives; without the two largest it is still clear; the median moves little because the short drives were already accurate.

Claim line: calibrating the seam scale improves VGGT-Long at its small-chunk setting (30/15), in our pipeline and in its own code, with no extra inference. At larger chunks most drives still improve but the mean does not; the gain shrinks as chunks grow, since VGGT-Long's scale drift shrinks too (part 10).

Always stated with it: 11 drives of one dataset; corrections fitted on other KITTI drives at the same chunk setting;
models do not transfer between chunk settings (part 13); the drives that got worse (part 14); KITTI ground-truth
height errors on 02, 08, 09 (documented by SemanticKITTI); without loop closure the gain is smaller and uneven
(parts 3 and 17).

## 6. Cost per setting (our pipeline)
| setting | peak GPU memory (GB) | summed wall time (h) | mean ATE VGGT-Long | mean ATE auto |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 30/15 | 9.5 | 1.75 | 45.66 | 35.35 |
| 60/30 | 11.9 | 2.10 | 25.82 | 25.00 |
| 75/30 | 13.1 | 1.33 | 24.61 | 25.37 |

Plain VGGT-Long at 75/30 (24.61 m) is more accurate than calibrated 30/15 (35.35 m with `auto`, 28.17 m with C4). What calibration offers at 30/15 is a smaller gap at lower peak memory, not a better result than large chunks.

## 10. Seam bias against chunk size (F4)
```
setting        frames/step  drives  seams  pooled_seam_bias  bias_per_frame  mean_drift_factor
first_w32_o16 (development)   16     10   1314   +0.0119 (se 0.0020)   +0.00074   x11.8
first_w30_o15                 15     11   1510   +0.0136 (se 0.0019)   +0.00091   x17.6
first_w60_o30                 30     11    752   +0.0102 (se 0.0026)   +0.00034   x2.4
first_w75_o30                 45     11    499   +0.0086 (se 0.0039)   +0.00019   x1.7
```
Per frame of step, the bias falls as chunks grow, and so does the drift without loops.

Mean seam log-scale error per drive (true / measured; positive = the map shrinks):
| setting | 00 | 01 | 02 | 03 | 04 | 05 | 06 | 07 | 08 | 09 | 10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 30/15 | +0.0114 | +0.0114 | +0.0141 | +0.0167 | +0.0460 | +0.0063 | +0.0082 | +0.0140 | +0.0145 | +0.0298 | +0.0101 |
| 60/30 | +0.0097 | +0.0043 | +0.0093 | +0.0147 | +0.0223 | +0.0014 | +0.0068 | +0.0149 | +0.0127 | +0.0248 | +0.0057 |
| 75/30 | +0.0110 | -0.0057 | +0.0059 | -0.0002 | +0.0319 | -0.0007 | +0.0071 | +0.0130 | +0.0120 | +0.0278 | +0.0043 |

At 30/15 every drive has a positive bias (+0.006 to +0.046), so one correction learned on other drives points the right way for all of them. At 75/30 the drive means run from -0.006 to +0.032, with 3 drives at or below zero (01, 03, 05), and the pooled bias is small (part 10 table above). At large chunks the seam scale error is mostly random from seam to seam, not a shared bias, and a calibration of the mean cannot remove random error. The oracle rows (part 7: true scale about 15 m at every setting) show the room a better seam scale estimate would still have.

## 11. Pixel weights in the alignment (F5)
Rule result: promising, not part of the method, future work; depth_only (no calibration) does about as well, so
the gain comes from the depth term, not from calibration.
